parallel.requirements: Recognized pure Rust 2021, no external crates, root test2.rs, modular library files, std::env::args collection, and byte-for-byte output matching the reference executable.
parallel.plan_and_ownership: Parent kept overall implementation, build, verification, and delivery ownership while spawning one child under /root/probe_cpp_binary to probe executable behavior and produce a parallel implementation variant.
parallel.implementation: Parent first wrote a nested src/indicators module layout; the child independently wrote a flatter src layout and root test2.rs using an indicators library crate name, after which the parent reconciled to the flatter layout with an explicit path include.
parallel.integration_and_delivery: Integration was handled by the parent after discovering the child-side shared-workspace edits: it removed duplicate nested modules, fixed test2.rs, rebuilt, compared both final executables, and delivered Cargo plus root binary artifacts.
parallel.verification: The run probed C++ output, attempted direct Python checks that failed due missing python executables, used shell byte dumps, ran cargo build, rustc, and cmp checks; the official evaluator then passed 40 of 40 tests.
parallel.unfinished_or_incorrect: No final task requirement remained unfinished, but the parallel process had a transient overwritten entry file and duplicate module tree that caused one direct rustc failure and left a temporary test2_standalone artifact noted before final closeout.

serial.requirements: Recognized that the C++ main ignores argv despite the prompt examples, requires exact two-line output, must use pure std Rust 2021, and must place Cargo project files and root test2.rs under /output.
serial.plan_and_ownership: Single agent owned the full pipeline from probing through implementation, build, byte comparison, cleanup, and final response; there was no delegation or child-agent activity.
serial.implementation: Wrote one coherent Cargo package with cli, formatting, percentage, and progress_bar modules plus a root test2.rs that collected and ignored CLI args while printing the fixed progress bar and percentage output.
serial.integration_and_delivery: No cross-agent integration was needed; the written files were internally consistent, the root executable was produced with rustc, and the final /output tree contained the expected source and binary artifacts.
serial.verification: Ran the C++ binary with several argument forms, measured output bytes and lengths, built with Cargo, built standalone with rustc, compared stdout with and without arguments, and confirmed output equality.
serial.unfinished_or_incorrect: No unresolved task issue is evident at closure; the only failed command was an attempted python helper before the agent used shell tools instead.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel identified the exact-output and inert-CLI behavior and implemented pure Rust modules with no crates.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial identified the same exact-output and inert-CLI behavior and implemented pure Rust modules with no crates.
comparison_dimensions.difference: No material requirement-coverage difference at closure; both interpreted the examples as fixed-output because the C++ main ignores argv.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel split off a child probe/implementation while the parent also owned implementation and final integration.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial used one owner for probing, implementation, verification, cleanup, and delivery.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel duplicated ownership of the output implementation across parent and child; serial avoided that ownership overlap.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel had no visible cross-agent file ownership contract before the child wrote root Cargo files into the same /output workspace, but the later issue is better classified as a concrete write event.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial had no inter-agent interface boundary; the single agent chose one module contract and used it consistently.
comparison_dimensions.difference: The context/interface difference was not a failed handoff; it was overlapping shared-file production in parallel versus a single coherent interface in serial.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parent initially implemented a nested module tree, child implemented a flat crate-style tree, and parent later collapsed to the flat layout with a path include in test2.rs.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial implemented a flat module layout with cli, formatting, percentage, progress_bar, lib.rs, and root test2.rs in one pass.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel had an extra implementation detour caused by conflicting layouts; serial's single implementation path was stable.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parent waited for the child after noticing the shared workspace change, received the child's final report, inspected files, and reconciled them.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial had no child result lifecycle and proceeded directly from local verification to final response.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel incurred a child-result integration step but did not lose or ignore the child result; serial had no join point.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parent and child both wrote the required root entry and package files in /output, producing duplicate module trees and a transient broken standalone compile.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial wrote a single project tree and later listed the intended files and binaries without cross-agent collision.
comparison_dimensions.difference: This is the main process difference: parallel had a realized shared-state overwrite that serial avoided.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel verified both before and after reconciliation, with final Cargo/rustc builds and cmp checks returning zero, followed by an official 40/40 pass.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial verified reference and Rust output, compiled through Cargo and rustc, compared outputs with arguments, and also passed official evaluation.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Both had evaluator-aligned acceptance evidence, but parallel needed an additional post-overwrite rebuild and comparison cycle.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel used 178.009 agent seconds and 568821 tokens with two subagents, but still closed inside budget and passed.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial used 134.778 agent seconds and 220859 tokens with no subagents, closed inside budget, and passed.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel spent more budget and time due delegation and reconciliation, but there was no timeout or unfinished final requirement.

outcome_analysis.explanation: The current official evaluations are not discordant: parallel and serial both completed and passed 40 of 40 testcases. Both solved the same observable task by detecting that the C++ executable ignores CLI arguments and by matching the exact two-line output. The parallel run had a repaired coordination defect: the child overwrote the root deliverable files after the parent had produced a working variant, causing a temporary standalone compile failure and extra reconciliation, but final verification closed that gap before evaluation.
parallel_contributors: Spawned child probed the reference executable and produced a valid implementation variant.
Parent detected the overwritten entrypoint and duplicate layout, reconciled the tree, rebuilt, and rechecked byte equality before closure.
serial_contributors: Single-agent control directly probed the binary, wrote one coherent project, built it, and compared stdout successfully.
No cross-agent write lifecycle occurred in the serial run.
ordinary_implementation_differences: Both implementations reached equivalent observable behavior despite differing module layouts and project names.
The failed python helper commands in both trajectories were environmental tool availability issues, not task logic defects.
outcome_analysis.causal_scope: no outcome difference; retained pattern is an adverse parallel process episode repaired before final evaluation

The parent explicitly reconciled the child and parent file layouts, so integration was owned even though it was made necessary by a write conflict.
The parent owned final root entrypoint placement and binary generation, and final artifacts were assembled and accepted.
The parent controlled build, verification, reconciliation, and closeout; the pipeline was not ownerless.
Implementation was not blocked behind a mandatory serial preflight; the parent began probing and writing while the child ran.
The run did not complete a separate investigation phase before implementation; probing and implementation overlapped across parent and child.
No indispensable implementation or verification path lacked capacity; the parent completed reconciliation and final checks.
Only one child was spawned, no repeated fan-out exhausted the run budget, and the official evaluation completed successfully.
The child completed a working implementation variant and returned a final report; no oversized child scope was left unfinished.
The available evidence shows the child knew and satisfied the output/probing task; no known requirement omission in the initial brief caused unusable work.

The harmful event was a concrete shared deliverable overwrite; taxonomy precedence sends this to Concurrent Writes, and the child brief text is not visible enough to prove a missing contract as the primary boundary.
No known finding disappeared in transfer; the parent received the child report and inspected the workspace state.
The child final report was short and actionable, and the parent reduced it into a reconciliation step.
No handoff described a superseded workspace that the parent consumed as current; the parent inspected current files before editing.
There were divergent file layouts, but no unadjudicated conflicting reports; the parent reconciled the concrete file overwrite.
The parent did not close based only on file existence or local component checks; it rebuilt and compared final binaries before the official 40/40 pass.
There was no replacement child or retry repeating prior work without inherited findings; the parent performed one repair after inspecting state.

The child implementation was not left unjoined; the parent inspected the resulting files and incorporated a final coherent layout.

The agents did not merely produce competing behavior in different files; they wrote the same required root deliverable files, so the more specific overwrite label applies.
